Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: 
The test `testContainsNone_StringWithSupplementaryChars` checks if the StringUtils.containsNone method correctly handles supplementary Unicode characters (characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane encoded as surrogate pairs in UTF-16). Specifically, it tests with U+20000 and U+20001, supplementary characters represented as surrogate pairs.

The bug report explains that StringUtils methods do not handle Unicode 2.0+ supplementary characters correctly and incorrectly match supplementary characters.

Looking at the implementation of `StringUtils.containsNone(CharSequence cs, String invalidChars)`, it converts the invalidChars string into a char array and calls the overloaded `containsNone(CharSequence cs, char[] searchChars)` method.

The `containsNone(CharSequence cs, char[] searchChars)` method loops over the characters in the input cs by index and checks each character individually against the searchChars by character. It does not take surrogate pairs into account; it only compares chars individually. This means for supplementary characters represented as two chars (high surrogate and low surrogate), the method treats each char separately.

Because of this, the method fails to correctly recognize supplementary characters as single code points and consequently may incorrectly match or fail to match characters in supplement planes.

Hence, the bug occurs because `containsNone` only handles BMP (Basic Multilingual Plane) characters and does not properly process surrogate pairs as single supplementary code points. This causes incorrect behavior when handling Unicode supplementary characters like U+20000.

This diagnosis matches the reported failure in the test that uses the supplementary chars \uD840\uDC00 and \uD840\uDC01.

Recommended next steps would be to inspect or fix methods handling supplementary characters in `StringUtils.containsNone`.

org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils.containsNone(java.lang.CharSequence, java.lang.String)
